title: Uber Backend (Educational Architecture)
description: Built an educational C++ backend inspired by Uber’s architecture using a custom modular framework. Implemented three multithreaded microservices and centralized logging via a Singleton pattern for clarity, maintainability, and observability.
details: Built three microservices for rider requests, driver matching, and trip updates, each running with multithreaded request handling.
Used gRPC and HTTP endpoints with Protobuf contracts to keep service communication structured and easy to extend.
Added Kafka and RabbitMQ integrations to model event-driven workflows for ride state updates and async processing.
Implemented a shared Singleton logger with file and console outputs for better debugging and observability during development.

title: Uber Rider App (Frontend)
description: Designed and developed a rider-facing Flutter app integrated with a modular C++ microservices backend. Implemented JWT-based authentication, real-time ride status tracking, and location updates with maps integration.
details: Designed rider flows for sign-in, ride booking, driver tracking, and trip completion with reusable Flutter widgets.
Integrated secure JWT authentication so user sessions are validated against backend APIs.
Connected real-time ride status updates to keep the UI synchronized with backend trip events.
Added map-based pickup and route views to improve rider visibility and booking accuracy.

title: C++ Modular Framework
description: Created a high‑performance C++ framework for distributed systems with integrated Kafka, RabbitMQ, and Uber H3 for geospatial indexing. Includes a robust utilities toolkit and a Singleton Logger for console/file logging.
details: Created a reusable C++ foundation layer for building backend services with consistent project structure and shared utilities.
Bundled integrations for Kafka, RabbitMQ, and H3 geospatial indexing to speed up distributed-system prototyping.
Added logging, config helpers, and common utilities so new services can start quickly with less boilerplate.
Packaged dependencies through Conan to keep builds reproducible across development environments.

title: WhatsApp UI Clone (Mobile)
description: Replicated the core WhatsApp interface to demonstrate UI/UX implementation and component-based mobile architecture.
details: Recreated key WhatsApp screens including chat list, chat room, and status-like layouts.
Built reusable React Native components to keep styling and behavior consistent across screens.
Focused on spacing, typography, and interaction details to match familiar messaging-app UX patterns.

title: Instagram Clone (Mobile)
description: Built a mobile clone with profile management, image upload/deletion, and post interactions (likes) to demonstrate full-stack mobile workflows.
details: Implemented profile and feed screens with post rendering and user interaction states.
Added create/delete post flows with image handling and backend API integration.
Used Redux for predictable state management across authentication, feed, and profile features.
Connected Node.js and MongoDB backend services to support persistent social interactions.

title: Plan + Approve Web-Search AI Agent (CLI)
description: Implemented a stateful AI agent that plans, pauses for approval, and conditionally performs web search. Used LangGraph for interrupt/resume, conversation summarization, memory checkpointing, and structured JSON planning with detailed logging.
details: Built a LangGraph-based agent workflow that creates plans, pauses for approval, and then continues execution safely.
Added interrupt/resume support with checkpoints so long-running sessions keep context across turns.
Implemented structured JSON plans and logging to make each decision traceable during debugging.
Integrated conditional web-search execution so the agent only calls search tools when needed.

title: eHealth Medical System (University Final Project)
description: Developed a full‑stack web and mobile platform for physiotherapists and clients to manage profiles, appointments, and medical reports with SDLC and unit testing.
details: Built web and mobile interfaces for therapists and clients to manage appointments and medical records.
Implemented role-based flows for profile updates, scheduling, and treatment report tracking.
Integrated Dockerized services and shared APIs to support consistent deployments across environments.
Applied SDLC documentation and unit testing practices as part of the final-year engineering process.

title: Employee Management System (University Group Project)
description: Built a centralized web application to streamline monthly payroll processing and automate payslip distribution.
details: Created payroll workflows for employee records, monthly salary calculations, and generated payslips.
Implemented a centralized management UI so administrators can update records from one place.
Added automation support for distributing payslip information with fewer manual steps.

title: CRUD Web Application
description: Created a web app for direct database manipulation through the UI to showcase CRUD operations and real‑time interactions.
details: Implemented full Create, Read, Update, and Delete operations through a simple frontend dashboard.
Connected React frontend forms and tables to Node.js API routes for live data updates.
Used MySQL for persistent storage and query-based record management.
